title: A lease and the margin at its end
request:
a one-second lease with a hundred milliseconds of clock error

./your_program.sh leases
init 1000 100
grant n1 0
read n1 899
read n1 900
read n1 1000
note: The lease runs to 1000 but the leader stops serving at 900. The hundred milliseconds it gives up are not waste: they are the amount by which its own clock might be behind, and serving into them is how two leaders end up answering reads in the same instant.

title: The window at the other end
request:
a second node asking for the lease at and after the nominal expiry

./your_program.sh leases
init 1000 100
grant n1 0
grant n2 1000
grant n2 1099
grant n2 1100
note: Granting at 1000 looks obviously safe and is not: the old holder's clock may be running a hundred milliseconds slow, so it can still believe the lease is live. The error budget is spent twice — once shortening the holder's window and once lengthening the granter's wait.
